what_happened.line: The Agricultural Commission tabled its recommendation of an applicant for the new Economic Development Committee, passing the task to two new members to find an agricultural candidate.
Members approved the January and February minutes at the first remotely held, publicly recorded meeting of the Commission.
Farmers market managers said most of the extra COVID expense was covered by vendor fees, and plexiglass bought up front is being repaid by vendors as they earn.
One performer still needed to be paid through a form to the town clerk, with a town vendor number set up to speed repayment.
The next meeting was set for July 16th, and the meeting adjourned by roll call.

why_it_matters: The town's seat on the new Economic Development Committee for agriculture stays unfilled for now, so farm interests have no recommended voice there until a candidate is found.
The farmers market is covering its pandemic costs mostly from vendor fees, so the minutes show no call on the town budget for it at this meeting.
watch_next: Next Agricultural Commission meeting, July 16th, and whether an agricultural candidate is put forward for the Economic Development Committee.
